ENGLISH — MOCK EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

2. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

7. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only a describing word

8. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   B. goes
   C. went
   D. going

10. When practising Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)

14. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. where is the library

15. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. Only one word repeated
